rows.description: C4 duplicate invoice — same vendor, same amount, 28 days apart
rows.exception_summary: Potential duplicate invoice detected for Acme Supplies: INV-2024-089 matches INV-2024-072, same vendor, EUR 12,450 amount, 28 days apart, identical line items.
rows.recommended_action: AP team should review the duplicate alert, verify that INV-2024-089 and INV-2024-072 are indeed the same invoice, and if confirmed duplicate, void one invoice and document the action. If the invoices represent separate legitimate purchases, the AP team must record the business justification and release the payment block, ensuring that the person releasing the block is different from the individual who raised the alert to satisfy segregation of duties. Maintain the block until resolution is documented.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on policy criteria and the provided data evidence; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C1 three-way match violation — invoice EUR 500 above PO+GR
rows.exception_summary: Invoice EUR 18,500 vs PO EUR 18,000 shows variance EUR 500, exceeding the 3%/EUR 150 tolerance and triggering a payment block per policy.
rows.recommended_action: AP Manager should review the variance, obtain business justification, adjust the PO or request a credit note, and ensure the automatic payment block remains until resolution.
rows.limitations: This flag identifies a policy deviation and exposure amount; it does not constitute evidence of fraud or misconduct. Anomaly flag, not proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C3 approval-threshold splitting — two invoices from same vendor totalling $19,800 within 7 days
rows.exception_summary: High‑severity potential splitting detected: two invoices (INV-2024-301 EUR 9,900 and INV-2024-302 EUR 9,850) submitted by the same requester to Office Depot within 7 days, total EUR 19,750 exceeds the $10k secondary‑approval threshold.
rows.recommended_action: Escalate the case to Internal Audit within 2 business days as mandated by Section 6.1; the AP Manager should place a payment block on the invoices pending review; verify that the requester obtained appropriate single‑level approval; conduct a root‑cause analysis and consider remedial training or process reinforcement.
rows.limitations: This is an anomaly flag based on policy indicators and the provided data; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct and requires further investigation for confirmation.

rows.description: C5 SoD violation — AP Clerk who created invoice also removed payment block
rows.exception_summary: User JSMITH, who recorded invoice INV-2024-188, also removed the payment block on the same document, constituting a SOD-04 segregation‑of‑duties violation with a critical severity and €45,000 exposure.
rows.recommended_action: 1. Initiate a human review of the removal action to verify the role of JSMITH and confirm whether any compensating control (e.g., monthly external review) was applied. 2. Verify that a written justification was documented as required by Section 5.3. 3. If the removal was not performed by an AP Supervisor or AP Manager, re‑classify the event as a control exception and notify Internal Audit. 4. Review role assignments to ensure JSMITH does not hold both AP Clerk and AP Supervisor/Manager permissions without Finance Director approval. 5. Strengthen monitoring by ensuring the automated weekly SOD‑violation report is reviewed promptly by the Finance Director.
rows.limitations: This output flags an anomaly based on the provided evidence and policy; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C6 Benford's law anomaly — leading digit 9 at 41% vs expected 4.6%
rows.exception_summary: Benford's Law screening for FastPrint Ltd in Q3 shows the leading digit 9 appearing in 41% of 14 reviewed invoices (expected 4.6%). Severity is medium with an estimated exposure of EUR 8,300.
rows.recommended_action: PROPOSAL: AP team should conduct a detailed manual review of all FastPrint Ltd invoices for the quarter, verify amounts, dates, and vendor details, cross‑check for duplicates per Section 4.1 criteria, and document findings. If anomalies persist, escalate to Internal Audit for further analysis.
rows.limitations: The finding is based solely on a Benford's Law anomaly flag and a sample of 14 invoices; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C4 duplicate invoice — different document IDs, same vendor and amount, 18 days apart
rows.exception_summary: Duplicate invoice detected for vendor CleanPro Services: INV-2024-441 and INV-2024-467, each EUR 3,200, issued 18 days apart, triggering duplicate flag.
rows.recommended_action: AP team should review the two invoices, verify if they represent the same service. If confirmed duplicate, void one invoice and keep the payment block. If legitimate, document the business justification, have a different reviewer release the block, and close the alert.
rows.limitations: This is an anomaly flag based on matching criteria, not definitive proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C2 invoice before goods receipt — invoice posted 5 days before GR
rows.exception_summary: Invoice INV-2024-355 (EUR 22,000) was posted on 2024-08-01, five days before the Goods Receipt was recorded on 2024-08-06, creating a three‑way‑match exception for vendor Nordic Steel (severity: medium).
rows.recommended_action: PROPOSAL: AP Manager should verify whether a payment block was applied to INV-2024-355, obtain and document a business justification for the early invoice posting, and ensure the invoice is cleared only after the goods receipt is confirmed. If no block exists, apply the block, investigate the root cause, and reinforce training on three‑way‑match procedures.
rows.limitations: This flag identifies a control anomaly based on the available data; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C1 + C4 compound — both three-way match violation and duplicate flag on same vendor
rows.exception_summary: Two high‑severity anomalies were detected for Meridian Consulting: (1) Invoice INV‑2024‑500 shows a variance of EUR 750 exceeding the three‑way‑match tolerance (Section 3.3) – a payment block should be applied per Section 5.1; (2) INV‑2024‑500 matches INV‑2024‑488 for the same vendor, same amount (EUR 15,000) and within 12 days, meeting the duplicate criteria of Section 4.1 – a duplicate alert and block should be applied per Section 5.1.
rows.recommended_action: PROPOSAL: AP manager to review and confirm the payment block for INV‑2024‑500 due to tolerance breach; investigate the root cause of the variance and document justification if an exception is approved. For the duplicate case, initiate duplicate‑alert resolution workflow, verify which invoice is legitimate, and retain the other on block pending supplier confirmation. Ensure segregation of duties by having a second reviewer clear any blocked invoices (per SOD‑05).
rows.limitations: This report flags anomalies based on policy criteria and exposure data; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct, only an indication that controls were not satisfied and further investigation is required. Anomaly flag, not proof of fraud or misconduct.

rows.description: C4 duplicate — within EUR 1 tolerance; low exposure
rows.exception_summary: A low‑severity duplicate invoice alert was triggered for vendor Stationery World: INV‑2024‑601 (EUR 420.00) and INV‑2024‑598 (EUR 420.50) – a EUR 0.50 difference, which is within the EUR 1 tolerance defined in the duplicate‑check criteria.
rows.recommended_action: AP reviewer should examine the two invoices, verify vendor, amount, and dates, and determine if they represent a true duplicate. If duplicate, void one invoice; if legitimate, document the business justification and release the block using a different reviewer than the one who raised the alert, in accordance with segregation‑of‑duties.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on policy criteria; it does not constitute proof of fraud or misconduct without further investigation.

rows.description: C5 SoD + C3 threshold splitting — compound exception with critical severity
rows.exception_summary: AP Clerk RBROWN both created invoice INV-2024-700 and removed its payment block (SOD-04 violation) and submitted two invoices for Alpha Corp (EUR 14,200 and EUR 13,800) within 6 days from the same requester, indicating possible splitting to bypass the $10,000 secondary‑approval threshold. Total exposure EUR 28,000.
rows.recommended_action: Propose that Internal Audit be engaged to review RBROWN’s activities, that the removal of the payment block be reversed pending investigation, and that the two invoices be examined for possible splitting. Require the AP Manager to document any approvals and ensure segregation of duties compliance before any further payment actions.
rows.limitations: This finding is an anomaly flag based on the provided evidence and policy; it does not constitute definitive proof of fraud or misconduct.
